import Mathlib

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def insertionSort_precond (v : List Int) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  True
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
def insertInt (a : Int) : List Int → List Int
  | [] => [a]
  | b :: bs =>
      if a ≤ b then
        a :: b :: bs
      else
        b :: insertInt a bs

def insertionSortAux : List Int → List Int
  | [] => []
  | a :: as => insertInt a (insertionSortAux as)
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definitions
def insertionSort (v : List Int) (h_precond : insertionSort_precond v) : List Int :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  insertionSortAux v
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def insertionSort_postcond (v : List Int) (result : List Int) (h_precond : insertionSort_precond v) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
   List.Sorted (· ≤ ·) result ∧ result.Perm v
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
theorem mem_insertInt (x a : Int) (l : List Int) :
    x ∈ insertInt a l ↔ x = a ∨ x ∈ l := by
  induction l with
  | nil =>
      simp [insertInt]
  | cons b bs ih =>
      by_cases h : a ≤ b
      · simp [insertInt, h]
      · simp [insertInt, h, ih, or_assoc, or_left_comm, or_comm]

theorem sorted_insertInt (a : Int) {l : List Int}
    (hsorted : List.Sorted (· ≤ ·) l) :
    List.Sorted (· ≤ ·) (insertInt a l) := by
  induction l with
  | nil =>
      simp [insertInt]
  | cons b bs ih =>
      rcases List.sorted_cons.mp hsorted with ⟨hb, hs⟩
      by_cases hab : a ≤ b
      · simp only [insertInt, if_pos hab]
        apply List.sorted_cons.mpr
        constructor
        · intro x hx
          simp only [List.mem_cons] at hx
          rcases hx with rfl | hx
          · exact hab
          · exact le_trans hab (hb x hx)
        · exact hsorted
      · simp only [insertInt, if_neg hab]
        apply List.sorted_cons.mpr
        constructor
        · intro x hx
          rw [mem_insertInt] at hx
          rcases hx with hxa | hx
          · subst x
            omega
          · exact hb x hx
        · exact ih hs

theorem insertInt_perm (a : Int) (l : List Int) :
    (insertInt a l).Perm (a :: l) := by
  induction l with
  | nil =>
      simp [insertInt]
  | cons b bs ih =>
      by_cases h : a ≤ b
      · simp only [insertInt, if_pos h]
        exact List.Perm.refl _
      · simp only [insertInt, if_neg h]
        exact List.Perm.trans
          (List.Perm.cons b ih)
          (List.Perm.swap a b bs)

theorem insertionSortAux_sorted (v : List Int) :
    List.Sorted (· ≤ ·) (insertionSortAux v) := by
  induction v with
  | nil =>
      simp [insertionSortAux]
  | cons a as ih =>
      simp only [insertionSortAux]
      exact sorted_insertInt a ih

theorem insertionSortAux_perm (v : List Int) :
    (insertionSortAux v).Perm v := by
  induction v with
  | nil =>
      simp [insertionSortAux]
  | cons a as ih =>
      simp only [insertionSortAux]
      exact List.Perm.trans
        (insertInt_perm a (insertionSortAux as))
        (List.Perm.cons a ih)
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem insertionSort_postcond_satisfied (v : List Int) (h_precond : insertionSort_precond v) :
    insertionSort_postcond v (insertionSort v h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  constructor
  · exact insertionSortAux_sorted v
  · exact insertionSortAux_perm v
  -- !benchmark @end proof

The student implements insertion sort directly:

- `insertInt` recursively inserts an integer into its appropriate position in an already sorted list.
- `insertionSortAux` recursively sorts the tail and then inserts the head into that sorted result. This is a standard recursive insertion-sort implementation and matches the required approach of inserting each element into a sorted prefix/suffix-built result.
- `insertionSort` invokes this implementation rather than a built-in sorting routine.
- The supporting lemmas establish preservation of membership, sortedness after insertion, permutation after insertion, and then sortedness and permutation for the complete algorithm.
- The final theorem proves both required postconditions.
